items.title: Show HN: Weir – Catch credential leaks in the AI agents you build and use
items.contentSnippet:
Hi HN. Weir is for one problem: credentials crossing the boundaries of your AI agent.
For agents you build, Weir plants fake credentials where real ones would live, runs the agent's normal flows, and checks what comes out: telemetry, logs, console output, model requests, and requests to other services. It looks for those exact values, including common encoded forms, and reports where they went without printing the credential.

items.title: Show HN: MacID – Bringing Face ID to the Mac
items.contentSnippet:
Hi HN! Since Macs have no Face ID, I built MacID: look at the webcam, press Return on the lock screen and you’re in. It runs fully on device and  if anything fails, TouchID and the password prompt still work.
However, since a webcam isn’t a depth sensor, a good photo can fool it (so I include a “require a blink” option).
Free & open source: https://macid.akshith.io

items.title: Show HN: Cryo – A language whose programs live forever
items.contentSnippet:
Cryo is a programming language that models long-running tasks like workflows or AI agents. Programs freeze to disk when idle and can be thawed when new data arrives.
As part of our announcement of Endothermic Labs, we've put together a small demo of Cryo that highlights its features and walks through the language and its plugin system.
We originally built it as a way to deploy healthcare agents at scale, but have rebuilt it from the ground up to be a standalone toolchain for long-running tasks.

items.contentSnippet:
Hi HN. GIFUP was an avatar and glitter generator I ran from 2007; it made about 1.3M animations before the web moved on. items.title: Give Families a Window Into What Students Are Really Learning
items.contentSnippet: Report cards show what students earned. They rarely show what students care about, how they think, or what they can do. In this practical piece from PBLWorks leaders Ryan Sprott and Taya Tselolikhina, district leaders will find concrete strategies for making student learning visible to families through project-based work, student-led exhibitions, and authentic communication channels. It is a timely read for any leader looking to move family engagement from passive updates to genuine partnership.
